To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ADP-ribose transferase inhibitor is present in the postribosomally derived supernatant of rat liver cells and is able to protect eEF-2 from ADP-ribo-sylation.

(i) eEF-2 isolated from rat liver undergoes ADP-ribosomal modification by the action of diphtherial toxin or endogenous eEF-2-ADP-ribosyllating enzyme, (ii) the ADP-ribose modification of eEF-1 and eEF-2 results in their irreversible inactivation and (iii) eEF-1 is not a substrate of endogenous transferases.
the cytoplasmic fraction of the postribosomal rat liver extract contains an inhibitor of eEF2 ADP-ribose transferase activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a cytoplasmic inhibitor, which is probably responsible in part for the lack of the lethal activity of the endogenous ADP ribosyltransferase in the cell.
the identification of a cytoplasmic protein which inhibits eEF-2 inactivation catalyzed by endogenous transferase or diphtheria toxins.
the discovery of the mechanism by which cells protect their protein synthesis machinery from the toxic effects of ADP-ribosylnation of the eEF-2 catalyzed by the endogenous ADP ribosyl transferase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytoplasmic inhibitor protects eEF-2 from ADP- ribosylation and inactivation by endogenous transferase. [on SciFinder (R)]
the rat liver cells possess a factor which inhibits the ADP- ribosylation of eukaryotic elongation factor 2 catalyzed by the diphtheria transferase and/or endogenous transferases.
the rat liver cells contain an inhibitor of the endogenous eEF-2 transferase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytoplasmic inhibitor is a factor which is able to prevent the lethal effect of ADP-ribosomal inactivation of eEF- 2.
ADP-ribosomal eEF-2 inactivation in the cytosol of rat liver cells is controlled by the inhibitor of endogenous transferases.
the fraction isolated from the rat liver extract is a cytoplasmic inhibitor which protects eEF-2 against irreversible ADP-ribosylation and inactivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ADP-ribose moiety of NAD+ is transferred to eEF-2 by endogenous transferase.
the ADP-ribose moiety is not transferred to eEF-2 in the presence of rat liver extract, which may be due to the presence of a cytoplasmic inhibitor.
the fraction from rat liver extract inhibits the ADP-ribose transferase and protects eEF-2 against its inactivation.
